class.name: NetwJoinRoster
class.brief_description: Who this peer has admitted, who it refused and why, and how it settles two players arriving under one name.
class.description: The two books move together. A peer remembered as accepted while a refusal reason still names it is a peer the session disagrees with itself about, so [method forget] erases both and there is no way to erase one. It holds no [Object] and disconnects nobody. A name collision is answered as a verdict the caller carries out, which is what lets the same rule decide for a join arriving on the wire and for one a test hands in directly. [codeblock] match roster.name_verdict(name, taken, rj.is_debug, has_identity): NetwJoinRoster.RENAME: rj.username = roster.free_name(name, taken) NetwJoinRoster.REFUSE: roster.refuse(rj.peer_id, reason) disconnect(rj.peer_id) [/codeblock] Every answer is in peer order, because a roster backfill and the roster it backfills have to agree about order and a hash walk does not.

method.name: accepted_join
method.description: The join record remembered for [param peer_id], or [code]null[/code] when none is.

method.name: accepted_joins
method.description: Every remembered join, in peer order.

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every peer at once, which is what a session teardown asks for.

method.name: forget
method.description: Forgets [param peer_id] from both books. There is deliberately no way to forget one and keep the other.

method.name: free_name
method.description: The first name of the form [param name] followed by a number that nobody in [param taken] holds, counting from one. What a [constant RENAME] verdict is carried out with.

method.name: name_verdict
method.description: How a join asking for [param name] is settled against the names in [param taken], as one of [enum Verdict]. [param is_debug] and [param has_identity] are the two things about the joining peer that change the answer, and they are asked in that order: a debug build renames rather than colliding at all, and only an authenticated peer can lose a name to somebody else's claim.

method.name: refusal
method.description: Why [param peer_id] was refused, or an empty string when it was not.

method.name: refuse
method.description: Records why [param peer_id] was refused. Recording is all this does: dropping the connection belongs to the caller that can reach the peer.

method.name: remember
method.description: Remembers one accepted join, answering whether the roster learned anything. A peer already remembered is remembered again only when the new record carries args the old one lacked, which is what keeps a roster backfill from replacing a real join with its argless echo.

method.name: serialize_accepted
method.description: Every remembered join serialized, in peer order, which is what a backfill sends.

constants.constant: Nobody holds the name, or somebody does and the session says so without stopping the join. An unauthenticated claim is not proof the name belongs to whoever made it first.
A debug join takes the next free name instead of the one it asked for, so two developers running the same build both get in.
An authenticated name belongs to whoever authenticated it, so the second claim is turned away.
